scope: reload acceptance trial with a bound controller's restart episode across the handovers; release binaries built from the reload integration branch (uncommitted merge, tree recorded); private daemon under a disposable home

source.note: the merge of fence-bindings, main and the reload stack tip, with the store's deferred data migrations and the trial's controller scenario; committed as the next commit on the branch

scenarios: 384 messages sent through 20 reloads arrived once, in order; 0 send errors
133 agents launched (half stopped early) during the reloads all finished; 0 launch errors
both loggers' logs are contiguous across every reload
batch and PTY fixtures exit with exact codes under the last daemon with complete logs
a lease and a pending question kept their identity and expiry across every switch; the question was answered after the last
a bound controller's restart episode ran to exhaustion across the handovers: 5 launches, attempts [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 19 handovers accepted in between
limits: The launched controller ends on its own after two seconds; a controller that starts and never binds (bind grace, SIGTERM, SIGKILL) is unit-tested, not trialled here.
Replay retention limits and Windows are not covered; provider-side acceptance (live Claude/Codex conversations across a switch) is codex's.

review_rerun.note: After the review fixes (deferred recovery takes its sequence numbers at the flush; Terminate revalidated under the guard; the successor pins its controllers before it answers serving; the trial ends its own processes and fails on any survivor), the same trial on the rebuilt release binaries.
review_rerun.warnings_note: Ten fenced-skip warnings on short agents' exits that landed during an offer; each exit was recovered after the acceptance, as the launches check requires (every launched agent reached a durable end).

retained_release_pin.scope: a disposable managed prefix and private daemon; a controller (a sleep, alive throughout) bound with a launch descriptor inside the first installed release, so nothing is ever launched from that release and only a daemon's pin for the binding can hold it; two later generations installed with the gated daemon handing over each time; a prune with the first release neither current nor previous; unbind with the token, and prune
scenarios: a bound controller's launch descriptor in the first release pins that release, with the controller alive and nothing launched from it
with the first release neither current nor previous, a prune keeps it while a controller's binding pins it
unbinding releases the pin, and the next prune removes the release
checks: the pin file for the first release is held by the first daemon while the bound controller is alive and nothing has been launched
after each handover, once the predecessor process is gone, the pin is still held, and the binding records no launched process
desktop prune --keep 0 --preview does not list the first release; after the prune its versions directory is still there
no warning in any daemon's log; the bound controller is still running at the end
unbind_input with the token releases the pin within ten seconds; the next prune removes the release
limits: The three generations are the same binaries with distinct package metadata, as the reload smoke's second generation is.

earlier_runs.note: The first two runs let the daemon launch `agentdocker events` from the first release after the bound controller was killed; a binary from that release then held its own executable pin, so those runs could not tell the successor's pin from the launched process's. Retained, not counted.

cleanup_rerun.note: Rerun after the trial's cleanup was made step-independent with survivor accounting; same source, same outcome.
